SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: DRESSING ENVIRONMENT
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES · Grade: PP2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Dressing ENVIRONMENT helps you succeed in ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: DRESSING ENVIRONMENT
Study Dressing ENVIRONMENT like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify clothes worn at • Learners to sort and group clothes different different times according to the occasion and ceremony occasions and

What this means
In this part you learn to identify clothes worn at • Learners to sort and group clothes different different times according to the occasion and ceremony occasions and. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify clothes worn at • Learners to sort and group clothes different different times according to the occasion and ceremony occasions and.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Dressing ENVIRONMENT” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify clothes worn at • Learners to sort and group clothes different different times according to the occasion and ceremony occasions and. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Dressing ENVIRONMENT is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Dressing ENVIRONMENT” around your school. (skill: identify clothes worn at • Learners to sort and group clothes different different times according to the occasion and ceremony occasions and)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Dressing ENVIRONMENT to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify clothes worn at • Learners to sort and group clothes different different times according to the occasion and ceremony occasions and.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Dressing ENVIRONMENT from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Dressing ENVIRONMENT: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP2 learner study Dressing ENVIRONMENT?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we put on c) to put on shoes correctly ceremony clothes?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Dressing ENVIRONMENT means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify clothes worn at • Learners to sort and group clothes different different times according to the occasion and ceremony occasions and.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
